This project is CommonJS and we are moving it to ES modules. Convert all of it: the 34 modules under src/ (including src/plugins/ and src/ring/), bin/cli.js, run-tests.js and the files in test/ (harness.js and the four *.test.js files). Then do Part 2 below.

Part 1, the conversion. Rules:
1. Rename every .js file to .mjs (same folder, same base name) and remove the old .js file. Do not add "type": "module" to package.json, and do not add dependencies.
2. Use import and export. Every relative import must include the full file name with the .mjs extension.
3. Export names stay exactly the same as today. A module that sets module.exports to one function or one class becomes a default export. A module that exports an object of names (module.exports = { ... } or exports.name = ...) gets the same names as named exports and no default export. A module that sets module.exports to a function and then attaches more properties to it (module.exports.name = ...) gets the function as the default export and each attached property as a named export. src/index.js exports the objects strings, numbers, arrays, objects and stats and the value VERSION; keep exactly those names.
4. Behavior stays the same, except for two changes that ES modules force. loadPlugin(name) in src/pluginLoader.js loads a plugin with a computed require; make it an async function that returns a promise for the plugin's default export (use a dynamic import). listPlugins() must still return the plugin names without an extension, sorted. And paths.thisFile() now returns 'paths.mjs', because it reports the module's own file name. __dirname and __filename do not exist in ES modules; Node 24 provides import.meta.dirname and import.meta.filename.
5. src/config.js loads data/defaults.json and src/limits.js loads data/limits.json; keep loading those same files and do not change them.
6. bin/cli.mjs must still run its command line when started with `node bin/cli.mjs sum 1 2 3` and must not run it when another module imports it. It still exports main.
7. ES modules always run in strict mode, and some code in this project only works in sloppy mode. Fix such code so that it still does what it did, without changing what the module exports and without leaving anything behind on globalThis.
8. A require() call inside a function body (src/registry.js) becomes a normal import at the top of the module. src/tree.js and src/walker.js import each other, and so do the three modules in src/ring/. Each of those cycles must work whichever of its modules is loaded first.
9. The "test" script in package.json must be `node run-tests.mjs`. Running `node run-tests.mjs` must run all 21 existing tests and exit with code 0. Keep all 21 tests.

Part 2, the plugin command line. This builds on the converted code.
10. loadPlugin(name) must reject with an Error whose message is `unknown plugin: <name>` when name is not one of the names listPlugins() returns. That includes names that reach other files, such as '../paths'.
11. bin/cli.mjs also exports an async function mainAsync(argv) that resolves to the same { code, out } shape as main. `plugins` prints the plugin names one per line. `apply <plugin> <text...>` loads the plugin, calls it with the remaining arguments joined by single spaces and prints the result. With a plugin name that is not listed, the result is code 2 and `unknown plugin: <name>`. With no plugin name or no text, it is code 2 and `usage: apply <plugin> <text>`. Every other command behaves as main does. main itself stays synchronous and unchanged. When bin/cli.mjs is started directly it must use mainAsync, so `node bin/cli.mjs plugins` and `node bin/cli.mjs apply title hello big world` work. Non zero codes still print to stderr.
12. The project already has a third plugin, src/plugins/title.js, whose function capitalizes the first letter of every space separated word. Convert it like the others. After the conversion listPlugins() returns ['reverse', 'title', 'upper'].
13. Add test/plugins.test.mjs with at least 3 tests that use the harness, import loadPlugin from src/pluginLoader.mjs and mainAsync from bin/cli.mjs, and pass. `node run-tests.mjs` must then run at least 24 tests, all passing.

When you are done, no .js file should remain in the project and no file should use require, module.exports, exports.x = , __dirname or __filename.
